rationale: Choose structure as a prospective history-free geometry hypothesis, not an established winner. The ligand target is the original bound ligand's heavy-atom cloud; the repulsion target is separation from the original receptor crop using the registered 2 A threshold. Neither requires generated Steer coordinates, score weights, selected teachers or parent-child history. Unit anchoring and stronger repulsion are provisional geometry safeguards, not fitted effect sizes. Disable the untyped contact term because pair-kernel enrichment does not establish receptor-contact benefit. A constant ramp avoids deriving stage rules from unsupported temporal summaries; the 0.2 native RMS ratio is a conservative permitted intervention. Use FLOWR endpoint VJP with detached Hungarian correspondence. Evaluate final predicted target pIC50 and strain against matched pocket and historical-family controls. Increment matching is not registered here and its coordinate definitions and support are incomplete, so no increment term is introduced.
failure_modes: Original ligand geometry may be unsuitable for generated graph transitions or may constrain useful alternative poses.
Hungarian correspondence switches can make the reward locally nonsmooth; detached correspondence requires consistent coordinate frames.
Untyped 2 A repulsion can miss chemically relevant clashes and penalize legitimate close contacts.
Constant guidance may have unsuitable timing; supplied temporal contrasts do not establish an alternative schedule.
Gradient normalization can cancel whole-reward scaling; relative component weights still alter direction.
Geometry improvement need not improve predicted pIC50, strain or physical binding affinity; matched prospective comparison is required.
